title: Choose the visual world for EV Readiness Check
question: Re-rolled for a vibrant, exciting look for a tech-forward, eco-minded family. The roll assigned Gear Spec. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Gear Spec
options.lineage: outdoor-gear catalogs: technical colorways and spec callouts
options.thesis: Your EV readiness as a spec sheet for your actual life: the loaded family car, with every number that matters called out.
materials: leader-line callouts on a family-EV side view
options.viewport: Navy top bar; a teal color field with the verdict in big condensed type; beside it a citron line drawing of a loaded family EV (car seat, dog crate, roof box) with four numbered callouts: charging 3.9 mi, range 45 mi, cost ~$520 a year, Rocky Mountain NP 36 mi; four color-blocked spec cards below keyed to the callouts.
options.risk: Outdoor-catalog styling can tip into selling a lifestyle; the vehicle drawing must stay generic, brandless, and honest.

raised.raise: Matched keys: each callout on the vehicle carries the same number and color as its spec card.
Tabular truth: every figure sets in tabular numerals with its unit, never rounded into vagueness.
Size by weight: the five factors' markers scale with their weight, so what matters most reads biggest.
One mile scale: your range need and every vehicle's range draw on one shared scale.
Strict type scale: one display family at four fixed sizes, nothing in between.

options.label: Family Transit Map
options.thesis: Your week as a transit map: commute, school run, and park trips as colored lines, with chargers as the stations they pass.
options.viewport: Verdict at top left; a map of four colored lines meeting at Home (80302), passing the fast charger at 3.9 mi and ending at Rocky Mountain NP at 36 mi; spec cards on the right.
options.risk: My top-ranked idea and a well-worn infographic trope; too many lines turns busy instead of clear.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.thesis: Every decision as an overhead yellow sign band: the verdict, then only the next choices, with distances.
options.viewport: A yellow band with the verdict and an arrow to Get my EV plan; distance bands below for charger, range, and park.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins on clarity for busy parents; loses audience identification, since it reads as travel rather than family, outdoors, and eco.
options.risk: One loud yellow can feel like a warning rather than an invitation.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Barcode columns and sine lattices in pure black and white.
options.viewport: Results as a strobing data field.
options.case: Loses both axes: no color, and data art reads cold to a family deciding on a car.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Coarse pixel letterforms at poster scale.
options.case: Loses both axes: retro type nostalgia, not family EV readiness.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Thousands of stamp-sized cells keyed to a hall map.
options.viewport: Chargers as cells keyed to a map.
options.case: Loses both axes: dense newsprint, and a niche world for this audience.
options.kept: Matched keys between picture and list.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Importance as dot size on a navy chart.
options.viewport: Chargers plotted like stars around home.
options.case: Loses both axes: beautiful but nocturnal and abstract for a busy daytime family.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.viewport: Readiness as stages on a shared baseline.
options.case: Loses both axes: cream and quiet, the opposite of the brief.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean EV-calculator look, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Verdict card with a green gauge, stat tiles for charging, range, and cost, and a green primary button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every EV calculator by design.
